---
title: "Travel"
---

## Arrival

Please be aware that August 29 - 31 is a bank holiday weekend, so Birmingham 
city centre will be busy and public transport may be disrupted. On the Monday,
many places will operate Sunday opening times or be closed - in particular, 
most university buildings will be closed.

### Travel to the accommodation

Participants arriving at Birmingham airport are recommended to take the 
free Air-Rail Link monorail to Birmingham International train station, then 
catch a train to Birmingham New Street (single ticket £5.00 from the ticket 
machines at the station). 

Then catch an X20/X21/X22 bus from 
St Martin's Queensway (Stop NS3) between the station and the Bullring shopping 
centre (tap the payment machine with your contactless card/phone as you get on 
the bus, you'll be charged £3 for each single journey up to a daily cap of 
£5.50).

Stops are announced and displayed on the bus. Get off at

* Aston House for Chamberlain Hall (reception closes at 10pm)
* Vale Village for the Shackleton Building to check-in to Chamberlain Hall 
after 10pm (reception open 24 hours)
* Westmere for Peter Scott House/Edgbaston Park Hotel

Total journey time should be around 50 minutes. Trains and buses do run until 
late at night, but you may prefer Uber/Bolt from the airport in this case, 
which will take around 30 minutes and cost around £30.

### Arriving at Chamberlain Hall

Check in is from 4pm. If you arrive earlier, you can store your luggage at 
Chamberlain Hall. The accommodation is next to a small park with a lake that 
is a nice place to wait a  while if the weather is nice. Otherwise you 
can walk to the Shackleton building, go in at reception and keep walking towards 
"The Shack" a lounge/canteen where there are tables and chairs you can use (a 
few plugs if you search hard enough). There are two outlets:

* Costcutter (Sunday only, 12pm-6pm): a mini supermarket
* "Coffee & hot food" (Monday only, 10am-3pm): to find this cafe, keep walking 
through The Shack, go out the door at the other end and walk towards the doors 
to the outside - the cafe is on your right and there are some nice booth seats 
to your left.

You might also walk to the Edgbaston Park Hotel, see the next section.

### Arriving at Edgbaston Park Hotel/Peter Scott House

Check-in is at Edgbaston Park Hotel for both hotels from 2pm, you can store 
your luggage there. 

If you arrive early, you are recommended to wait in the cafe bar/lounge that is 
just beyond reception. There are plenty of plugs to charge up your laptop or 
phone. The bar opens at 9am, food is available from the bar menu:
breakfast from 9:30am-12pm, sandwiches 12pm-6:30pm, and salads, pizza and other 
main dishes from 12pm-9pm. Expect to pay £15-25 for a meal.

If you arrive earlier, or want something a bit cheaper, you can go to 
[Joe's](https://www.guildofstudents.com/joes/), a Wetherspoon's pub on campus 
that is open 8am-midnight.

## Things to Do

If you want something to do before the sprint, here are a few suggestions:

* [Birmingham Weekender](https://www.birminghamhippodrome.com/birmingham-weekender-2026-whats-on/) 
free festival of music and dance, across city centre venues (including New Street Station!)
* [Winterbourne House](https://www.winterbourne.org.uk) an Arts and Crafts villa and garden, a short walk from Edgbaston Park Hotel. There is also a cafe here open 10:30am - 4:30pm. Entrance may be free for people staying at Edgbaston Park Hotel and Peter Scott House, please enquire at reception.
* [Midlands Arts Centre](https://macbirmingham.co.uk/) a 10 minute bus ride on the number 1 bus from Chamberlain Hall. Next to [Cannon Hill Park](https://www.cannonhillpark.co.uk/), the MAC has some free exhibitions, a cafe and an arts cinema. There will be free live jazz and soul music 1pm-4pm on Monday 31 August.
